comment: Spoken Portuguese, the way the assistant is actually used. `accept` lists the tool names that count as correct; null means the model should call nothing. `args_contain` is checked as a subset, `args_absent` catches invented arguments. The SQLite task tools are registered under *_local_task names and their descriptions forbid use unless the user says 'local', so they never count as correct here. The :8003 slim server offers a second, lighter Nextcloud API; both it and the stream2 one count as correct.

cases.why: The default location is already in the schema. Passing coordinates means the model invented them.

cases.prompt: como vai ser o tempo essa semana?
cases.why: Daily vs weekly is the cheapest test of reading a description to the end.

cases.prompt: qual a previsão do tempo em Tóquio?
cases.why: The opposite case: here coordinates are mandatory, and the model has to know Tokyo's.
The local SQLite twin `list_local_tasks` says to use it only when asked for local tasks. Picking it is the failure being measured.

cases.prompt: cria uma tarefa pra comprar pão amanhã às 9 da manhã
cases.why: Argument extraction from loose speech, plus not falling into `create_local_task`.

cases.prompt: o que eu tenho na agenda hoje?
cases.why: Agenda and tasks are different tools and the words are close.

cases.prompt: quanto de energia eu estou gastando agora?
cases.why: Three energy tools differ only by description; state is the one with no arguments.

cases.prompt: marca a tarefa de comprar pão como concluída
cases.why: Has to pass the title through instead of asking for a UID, and not hit `complete_local_task`.
DIAGNOSTIC: both wake tools carry the same docstring, so only the name can disambiguate.
DIAGNOSTIC: same as above, from the other side.
Numbers have to survive the trip into the arguments.
A destructive tool should still be reached when it is what was asked — but the Nextcloud one, not the SQLite one.

cases.prompt: bom dia, tudo bem com você?
cases.why: Restraint. A greeting is not a tool call.
Restraint under keyword pressure: no tool answers this, and guessing one is the common failure.
